original_question: Solved problem record: is there a group with exactly a countable infinity of right orders?
target_in_paper: Section 2.2, Problem 2.18: "Is there a group with exactly a countable infinity of right orders?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact problem in the paper almost verbatim: it is an existential question about a group having exactly countably infinitely many right orders, and it belongs to the solved-problems list for right-ordered groups.
missing_details: The phrase "right orders" should be made explicit as meaning total orders on the group that are preserved by multiplication on the right (the Section 2 ambient notion).
It should say that the count is the number of distinct right orders on a single group G.
"A countable infinity" is best rendered as cardinality exactly ℵ0, to rule out any ambiguity with finite countability.

To be paper-faithful, it should stay in the right-order context only, not broaden to two-sided orders; the paper explicitly contrasts this question with the existence of groups having countably many two-sided orders.
Because this is a solved-problem record in the paper, a fully faithful record should note that the paper reports the answer is negative.
refined_question: Does there exist a group G such that the set of all distinct right orders on G—that is, total orders on G preserved by multiplication on the right—has cardinality exactly ℵ0?
justification: The draft matches Problem 2.18 in the paper essentially word for word. Section 2 sets the ambient scope as right-ordered/right-orderable groups and explains that the ordering is preserved by multiplication on the right. In Section 2.2, the paper states exactly this question and immediately records that the answer is no, citing Linnell [54]; it also notes, by contrast, that groups with countably many two-sided orders do exist. So the sharp stand-alone reformulation should simply define "right order" and clarify that the cardinality being counted is the full set of distinct right-invariant total orders on one group, without adding any extra hypotheses such as countability, finite generation, or solvability.
